translation: Target is defined to be the conjunction of five claims: (1) There exists an arithmetic axiom set F such that F is recursively enumerable and, for every arithmetic sentence σ, PA proves σ if and only if F proves σ. F need not be PA’s own axiom set; only their theorem sets must agree. (2) For every arithmetic sentence σ, if PA proves σ, then σ is true in the standard natural numbers. (3) The set of all PA theorems, taken as an axiom set, does not prove a contradiction. (4) The sentence saying that a contradiction is not provable from PA’s Craig presentation, using that presentation’s standard provability predicate, is true in the standard natural numbers. (5) That same sentence is not a PA theorem. The existential quantifier over F applies only to (1); the consistency sentence in (4) and (5) is formed from PA’s Craig presentation, not from F.

divergences.description: Def6 makes effective axiomatizability explicit: PA’s theorems must be exactly those of some recursively enumerable axiom set. The passage leaves this feature of a formal system implicit.
Def4 tests consistency using all PA theorems as axioms rather than PA’s original axioms. This does not change consistency, since taking deductive closure adds no new theorems.

The consistency sentence uses the provability predicate for PA’s Craig presentation. This presentation has exactly PA’s theorems, so the sentence expresses the right consistency condition, though it need not be syntactically identical to the sentence formed from PA’s original axioms.

judgement.summary: The target gives the claimed PA instance of item (c): it states that PA is sound and consistent and that the same arithmetic consistency sentence is true in the standard natural numbers but is not a PA theorem.
